spots.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Fri

spots.summary: The President Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a mausoleum which serves as the resting place of Vietnamese revolutionary leader and President Ho Chi Minh in Hanoi, Vietnam.

spots.name: Imperial Citadel of Thăng Long

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Imperial Citadel of Thăng Long is a complex of historic buildings associated with the history of Vietnam located in the centre of Hanoi, Vietnam. Its construction began in 1010 and was completed in early 1011 under the reign of Emperor Lý Thái Tổ of the Lý dynasty.

spots.name: Temple of Literature
spots.summary: Văn Miếu, literally translated as Temple of Literature, is a temple dedicated to Confucius in Hanoi, northern Vietnam. The temple was founded and first built in 1070 at the time of Emperor Lý Thánh Tông, and it hosted the Imperial Academy, Vietnam's first national university, from 1076 to 1779.

photo.author: The original uploader was Chuoibk at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Hỏa Lò Prison
spots.summary: Hỏa Lò Prison was a prison in Hanoi originally used by the French colonists in Indochina for political prisoners, and later by North Vietnam for U.S. prisoners of war during the Vietnam War. During this later period, it was known to American POWs as the "Hanoi Hilton".

spots.name: Hoàn Kiếm Lake
spots.summary: Hoàn Kiếm Lake, also known as Sword Lake or Tả Vọng Lake, is a fresh water lake, measuring some 12 ha in the historical center of Hanoi, the capital city of Vietnam.

spots.name: Flag Tower of Hanoi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Flag Tower of Hanoi is a tower in Hanoi, Vietnam, which is one of the symbols of the city and once a part of the Hanoi Citadel, a World Heritage Site. Its height is 33.4 m.

spots.name: Long Biên Bridge
spots.summary: Long Biên Bridge is a historic cantilever bridge across the Red River that connects two districts, Hoàn Kiếm and Long Biên of the city of Hanoi, Vietnam. It was originally called Paul Doumer Bridge.

spots.name: One Pillar Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The One Pillar Pagoda, formally belongs to an architecture complex called Diên Hựu tự which means 'pagoda of extended blessings'. The pagoda is a historic Buddhist temple in the central Ba Đình district, Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam.

spots.name: Turtle Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Turtle Tower, also called the Tortoise Tower, is a small tower in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake in central Hanoi, Vietnam. It is one of the most iconic, symbolic and most recognizable pieces of architecture representing Hanoi and the entirety of Vietnam.

spots.name: Saint Joseph Cathedral
spots.summary: St. Joseph's Cathedral is a Catholic church on Nhà Chung Street, in the Hoàn Kiếm District of Hanoi, Vietnam. It is a late 19th-century Gothic Revival church that serves as the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Hanoi. The cathedral is named after Joseph, the patron saint of Vietnam.

spots.name: Vietnam National Museum of History

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Vietnam National Museum of History is in the Hoan Kiem district of Hanoi, Vietnam. The museum building was originally a museum of the French School of the Far East during French colonial rule.

spots.name: Hanoi Train Street
spots.summary: Train Street or Railway Street is a narrow train bypass in Hanoi which several times daily sees a train pass close to buildings on either side of the tracks. It is situated specifically, along Điện Biên Phủ and Phùng Hưng streets, opposite Dropin Cafe and the main Hanoi Railway Station.

photo.author: Takeshi Aida from Hong Kong, Hong Kong

spots.name: Trấn Quốc Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Trấn Quốc Pagoda, the oldest Buddhist temple in Hanoi, is located on a small island near the southeastern shore of Hanoi's West Lake, Vietnam.

spots.name: West Lake
spots.summary: West Lake is the biggest freshwater lake of Hanoi, Vietnam, located northwest of the city center. With a shore length of 17 kilometres (11 mi) and 500 hectares (5.0 km2) in area, this is the largest lake of the capital and a popular place for recreation with many surrounding gardens, hotels and villas.

spots.name: Hanoi Opera House
spots.summary: The Hanoi Opera House, or the Grand Opera House is an opera house in central Hanoi, Vietnam. It is located at August Revolution Square, anchoring the head of Tràng Tiền street.

spots.name: Ba Đình Square
spots.summary: Ba Đình Square is the name of a square in Hanoi where president Ho Chi Minh read the Proclamation of Independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam on September 2, 1945. It is named after the Ba Đình Uprising, an anti-French rebellion that occurred in Vietnam in 1886–1887 as part of the Cần Vương movement.

spots.name: Thê Húc Bridge
spots.summary: Thê Húc Bridge, is a footbridge over Hoàn Kiếm Lake within Hanoi, Vietnam.

spots.name: Vietnam Military History Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Fri

spots.summary: The Vietnam Military History Museum, set up on 17 July 1956, is one of seven national museums in Vietnam.

spots.name: Ho Chi Minh Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Fri

spots.summary: The Ho Chi Minh Museum is located in Hanoi, Vietnam. Constructed in the late 1980s and opened in 1990, it is dedicated to the late Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh and Vietnam's revolutionary struggle against foreign powers.

photo.author: Aaron from san francisco, United States

spots.name: Lotte Center Hanoi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lotte Center Hanoi is a skyscraper in Ba Đình district, Hanoi, Vietnam. Completed on 2 September 2014, the tower has 65 floors.

spots.name: Vietnam Museum of Revolution

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Vietnam Museum of Revolution was a museum in Hanoi, Vietnam. It is now part of the Vietnam National Museum of History.

spots.name: Quán Thánh Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Quán Thánh Temple, also known as Trấn Vũ Temple, is a Taoist temple in Hanoi, Vietnam. Dated to the 11th century, the temple was dedicated to Xuan Wu, or Trấn Vũ in Vietnamese, one of the principal deities in Taoism.

spots.name: Stone stele records of imperial examinations of the Lê and Mạc dynasties
spots.summary: Stone stele records of imperial examinations of the Lê and Mạc dynasties is a collection of 82 stone stelae that contain the names and related information of doctoral laureates who passed the imperial examinations during the reign of the Lê and Mạc dynasties from 1442 to 1779.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Stone stele records of imperial examinations of the Lê and Mạc dynasties

spots.name: Kính Thiên Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kính Thiên hall was the throne hall built as the central structure of the imperial palace complex of the Later Lê dynasty, located in its capital Đông Kinh. The palace hall was renamed Long Thiên Palace in 1841 during the reign of Emperor Thiệu Trị of the Nguyễn dynasty.

spots.name: Lenin Park
spots.summary: Lenin Park, formerly known as Chi Lăng Flower Garden, is a park in Hanoi, Vietnam, named after Vladimir Lenin. It lies across from the Vietnam Military History Museum and is surrounded by the streets of Điện Biên Phủ, Trần Phú, and Hoàng Diệu.

spots.name: Vietnamese Women's Museum
spots.summary: The Vietnamese Women's Museum, is a museum established and operated by the Vietnam Women's Union, officially opened its doors to public in 1995. The four-storey building is in Hanoi, Ly Thuong Kiet Street, situated along the central Hoan Kiem Lake and old quarter.

spots.name: Vietnam National Museum of Fine Arts
spots.summary: The Vietnam National Museum of Fine Arts is located in Hanoi, Vietnam. It is a museum showcasing Vietnam's fine arts from a range of historical periods. It is the country's primary art museum, the second being the smaller Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Vietnam National Museum of Fine Arts

spots.name: Tonkin Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tonkin Palace, also known as State Guest House, is a historical monument in Hoàn Kiếm District, Hanoi, Vietnam. It is presently used as a state guest house for foreign affair activities, as well as the operational headquarter for the country's presidential office.

spots.name: Hữu Tiệp Lake
spots.summary: Hữu Tiệp Lake is a small artificial freshwater lake located in Ngọc Hà Ward, Hanoi.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Presidential Palace Historical Site
spots.summary: The Presidential Palace Historical Site, which is located in Hanoi, Vietnam, is the place where Ho Chi Minh lived and worked during most of his time as leader of North Vietnam, from December 19, 1954 until his death on September 2, 1969.

spots.name: Quán Sứ Pagoda
spots.summary: Quán Sứ Pagoda is a Buddhist temple located at 73 Quan Su Street, Hanoi, Vietnam. The temple is the headquarters of the Buddhist Sangha of Vietnam.

spots.name: Voi Phục Temple
spots.summary: The western temple, dedicated to Prince Linh Lang, a son of King Lý Thái Tông and his 9th concubine Dương Thị Quang, who was killed in action at the Battle of Như Nguyệt River in a war with China's Song Dynasty. The name Voi Phục means "kneeling elephant", and you can see two statues of elephants in a kneeling position at the front of the temple, hence its name.

spots.name: Vietnam People's Air Force Museum, Hanoi

hours.note: Closed Fri

spots.summary: The Vietnam People's Air Force Museum, Hanoi or Bảo Tàng Phòng Không - Không Quân is located on Truong Chinh Street in the Bach Mai District of Hanoi. The museum is on the edge of the disused Bach Mai Airfield.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Vietnam People's Air Force Museum, Hanoi

spots.name: Ngoc Lu drum
spots.summary: The Ngoc Lu drum is regarded as one of the most important and prominent artifacts of the Dong Son culture of the Bronze Age, a civilisation that flourished in around the 2nd to 3rd century BC in the Red River Delta of Vietnam.

spots.name: Hang Bong
spots.summary: Hàng Bông Street, formerly Rue du Coton during the French colonial period, is a street in ancient quarter of Hanoi. It continues from the crossroad Hàng Bông - Hàng Gai - Hàng Trong - Hàng Hom to the former city gate Cửa Nam with length about 932 m.

spots.name: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Vietnam Museum of Ethnology is a museum in Hanoi, Vietnam, which focuses on the 54 officially recognised ethnic groups in Vietnam. It is located on a 43,799-square-metre (10.823-acre) property in the Cầu Giấy District, about 8 km from the city center.

spots.name: Grand Palais

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grand Palais or Grand Palais de l'Exposition was an exhibition and trade fair complex in Hanoi, Vietnam. It was built for the 1902 Hanoi Exhibition world trade fair, as the city became the capital of French Indochina. It was completely destroyed by American airstrikes in World War II.

spots.name: Bach Ma temple

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The eastern temple, dedicated to Long Đỗ, the thành hoàng (city god) of Thăng Long (now Hà Nội), and represented in the temple as a white horse (Bạch Mã in Vietnamese, hence its name).

spots.name: Hanoi Citadel
spots.summary: The Imperial Citadel of Thăng Long is a complex of historic buildings associated with the history of Vietnam located in the centre of Hanoi, Vietnam. Its construction began in 1010 and was completed in early 1011 under the reign of Emperor Lý Thái Tổ of the Lý dynasty.

spots.name: Nguyễn Thái Học Street
spots.summary: Nguyễn Thái Học Street is a major street in Văn Miếu - Quốc Tử Giám Ward, Hanoi.

spots.name: Đại La
spots.summary: Đại La, means the Citadel of the Great Dike, or La Thành (羅城) was an ancient fortified city in present-day Hanoi during the third Chinese domination of the 7th and 8th centuries, and again in the 11th-century under Lý dynasty.

spots.name: National Library of Vietnam

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Library of Vietnam is the national library in Vietnam and it is located in Hanoi. It was established by a decree of 29 November 1917 as the central library of Indochina. In September 1919 the library was made open to the public with an intent to support and promote western archive and library work.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Cửa Bắc Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cửa Bắc Church is a Roman Catholic church in Hanoi, Vietnam. Originally named as Church of Our Lady of the Martyrs, the church was built in 1931 by the French administration of Indochina as a part of the Hanoi's urban plan supervised by Ernest Hébrard.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Al-Noor Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Al-Noor Mosque is a mosque in Hoàn Kiếm ward, Hanoi, Vietnam. It is the only mosque in Hanoi and northern Vietnam.

photo.author: Richard Mortel from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

spots.name: Mỹ Đình National Stadium
spots.summary: The Mỹ Đình National Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Từ Liêm Ward, Hanoi, Vietnam. It has a capacity of 40,192 seats and is the centerpiece of Vietnam's National Sports Complex.

photo.author: NamHyHoangPhong đã đưa vào phạm vi công cộng

spots.name: Vietnam War Memorial, Hanoi
spots.summary: The War Memorial in Hanoi is located across the Ba Đình Square, across the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and close to Hanoi Citadel.

spots.name: Hàm Long Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hàm Long Church, officially Church of St. Anthony of Padua, is a Roman Catholic church in the center district Hoàn Kiếm of Hanoi, Vietnam. The church was built at the end of the 19th century near an old street named Hàm Long from which Hàm Long Church was called.

spots.name: Quảng trường Cách mạng tháng Tám

photo.author: The original uploader was Fuzheado at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Hàng Đẫy Stadium
spots.summary: Hàng Đẫy Stadium, also known as Hanoi Stadium, is a multi-purpose stadium in Hanoi, Vietnam. It is currently used mostly for football matches. The stadium holds 22,500 spectators; however, due to the dilapidating condition, the upper level of stand B is currently unusable, reducing this number to approximately 15,000.

spots.name: Labour Square
spots.summary: Labour Square or 1-5 Square is a town square located in Hoàn Kiếm district, Hanoi, Vietnam.

spots.name: Lý Thái Tổ Statue & Park
spots.summary: The park faces Hoàn Kiếm lake, with a beautiful view of the busy Hang Bai St. and the serenity of the willows on the bank of the lake. Many locals view this mini-park as their favourite place because it is a symbol of the integration of modernity and tradition. One might encounter a group of youths practising hip-hop, breakdancing, or playing foot-badminton, while at the same time seeing a three-g

spots.name: Downed Aircraft Memorial
spots.summary: A stone plaque commemorating the shooting down of a US Navy (not "USAF" as depicted) aircraft in 1967. Read the Vietnamese script and you can pick out the name of John McCain, the late U.S. senator, one of the airmen.

spots.name: Canton Assembly Hall
spots.summary: Former assembly hall of the Chinese from Guangdong province. It was converted to a kindergarten after the 1979 Sino-Vietnamese War, but was restored to its former glory in 2021, and is now an exhibition space open to the public.

spots.name: Kim Liên Shrine
spots.summary: The southern temple, dedicated to Cao Sơn Đại Vương, a Vietnamese mountain god who is said to be a son of King Lạc Long Quân of the ancient Hồng Bàng dynasty and his wife, the immortal mountain snow goddess Âu Cơ.

spots.name: Bún Chả Đắc Kim
spots.summary: Some rate this as one of the best examples of bún chả in Hanoi, and therefore Vietnam (apparently in the south, bún chả is specifically advertised as Hanoi-style). For 100,000 dong each, you'll get a bowl full of tiny minced-pork rissoles that have been chargrilled over an open flame and a massive plate of pork rice paper rolls that have been fried in oil twice. You also get a phenomenal dipping s

spots.name: JW Café
spots.summary: Luxury buffet restaurant. Immense triple-height dining room with panoramic views of adjacent lake and National Convention Center complex. Six live stations serve Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Indian, Mediterranean, BBQ, carved meat and fresh seafood selection; Sunday brunch has unlimited abalone, lobsters, French oysters and foie gras. Attached "Chocolate Lab" makes fresh, handmade truffles on site.

spots.name: Stellar Steakhouse
spots.summary: Fine American steakhouse serving a wide range of aged meats, including authentic Japanese Kobe; named Asia's Best Luxury Steakhouse in the 2019 World Luxury Restaurant Awards. Glitzy Art Deco dining room with panoramic views of the city. Large private rooms, dedicated wine & cheese tasting room, and upstairs whisky & sake lounge. Attached mezzanine-floor Stellar Teppanyaki serves its own tasting m

spots.name: Sushi Uminohana
spots.summary: Authentic omasake restaurant in Hanoi's "Japantown", serving traditional sushi, sashimi and donburi; all seafood and Wagyu beef flown fresh from Japan multiple times per week. A favourite of local Japanese expats, head chef have decade's worth of experience in Japan and speaks fluent Japanese. No tables, only 12 counter seats. Second-floor Teppan Shu exclusively serves grilled Ozaki beef. Reservat

spots.name: Top of Hanoi
spots.summary: Large outdoor rooftop bar & brasserie with 128 seats. One of the highest bars in the world at 272 m, with commanding 360-degree views of the entire city, live DJs on Tu-Su, and open kitchen. Best visited at sunset for Golden Hour ambiance; can get quite chilly at night due to high altitude, especially during winter, so bring outerwear if necessary. Noticeably pricier than the average bar, as to be

spots.name: Tầm Vị
spots.summary: Vietnamese restaurant in well-preserved heritage villa, serving traditional Northern cuisine at reasonable prices. Excellent choice for first-time visitors who want authentic home-style cooking in a more upscale dining space. Inexplicably awarded a Michelin star in 2023 despite not at all being a fine dining destination, but forget about the star and you'll have a good time. To the restaurant's cr

spots.name: Việt Lai Thuận
spots.summary: Grand Chinese dining hall serving the best and most authentic Sichuanese cuisine in town, alongside some Cantonese options. Caters near-exclusively to Chinese group clientele, with private rooms and karaoke facilities. Servings are all very large (sized for 3-4 pax) as a result, but kitchen can accommodate requests for half-servings.

spots.name: Etēsia
spots.summary: Excellent contemporary European wine bar and bistro, with intimate countertop seating and dedicated cocktail bar on second floor. French head chef formerly sous chef at Michelin-starred Parisian restaurant. No tables, only 18 counter seats. Reservations recommended due to limited seating, but walk-ins also welcome.

spots.name: Dalcheeni
spots.summary: Authentic Indian restaurant with classy interior and good view of West Lake, frequented by Indian expats; restaurant manager is a Goa native. All meat served is halal, with extensive vegetarian options available. Highly recommend the tandoor-grilled chicken, lamb and broccoli dishes. Reservations recommended.

spots.name: Com Chay Nang Tam Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.summary: This excellent restaurant is a good vegetarian option, and will please both vegetarians and non-vegetarians with its wide range of innovative dishes, which include fake meat dishes. Restaurant is comfortable with good ambience, and is good value. Well worth the short walk out of the old town.

spots.name: Pepperoni's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Part of a small international chain of pizza restaurants. Locally run, they do regular special offers such as free desserts, eat-all-you-can buffets and loyalty schemes, whereby collecting tokens with each take-out entitles you to a free pizza. Pizzas, burgers, ice cream and apple crumble.

spots.name: dragonCELLO
spots.summary: Italian restaurant in grand colonial-style mansion, with commanding lakefront views of West Lake. Ground floor counter also offers extensive selection of Italian cured meats and cheese for takeaway. Risottos are especially good. Reservations recommended; home deliveries also available.

spots.name: Moon Men Cocktail Bar
spots.summary: Boutique cocktail bar on the top floor of a building with a balcony overlooking the cathedral. Menu covers homemade-infused signature cocktails as well as classics; non-alcoholic options available. Happy hour 17:00-20:00. Reservations accepted. Cash, card and QR payment.

spots.name: Ramen Haron
spots.summary: Hole-in-the-wall ramen joint in Hanoi's "Japantown", frequented by Japanese expats; some staff speaks Japanese. Excellent quality and variety of ramen at very reasonable prices. Reservations recommended due to limited seating; takeaway and home deliveries also available.
